_about: Rebuilder fair-value laws for CTC 2026 Hurricane Season (RECON, MAT, GEN). Fit seasons 1-400, holdout 401-600. Value = a + b*(1 - exp(-D/c)) with D cumulative over the SEASON (all storms so far, not per storm). VERIFIED copy (independent re-implementation in work/se/verify-rebuild): RECON/MAT/GEN laws confirmed; corrections listed under 'verification.corrections' and applied to the fields named there.
insured_loss_identity: industry_loss_musd(storm) = 9.0*PORT + 6.0*ISLE + 2.5*AQUA + 7.0*GRID + 1.2*FERRY (damage_pct of that storm); rmse 0.044 $M over 1800 storms

RECON.driver: D = sum over season storms of 9.0*PORT_pct + 7.0*GRID_pct + 1.2*FERRY_pct ($M of port+grid+ferry damage at insured value; ISLE/AQUA excluded)

MAT.driver: D = sum over season storms of 9.0*PORT + 6.0*ISLE + 2.5*AQUA + 7.0*GRID + 1.2*FERRY pct = season insured loss $M (= running sum of industry_loss_musd)

GEN.driver: D = sum over season storms and the 5 GRID substations of weight_i * seconds(real) with I*exp(-(d_i/r)^2) > 0.35 (substation closed); 120 real s = 1 market hour

wind_model.fit_from: impact messages, seasons 1-200: of 869 actual impacts, the first predicted crossing (integer ages, any site on the island) is within 0.5 s for 83.2% and within 2 s for 99.3%; 1 missed, 0 false alarms. (The earlier '93.9% within 0.5 s' counted the ~1530 storm-island pairs with no impact and no predicted crossing as exact matches.) Independent check: fitting theta directly on GEN settlements (train) gives a sharp minimum at 0.350 with exponent 2 (k=1); theta 0.345/0.355 or exponent scale 0.9/1.1 are 2-10x worse.
wind_model.closure_integration: int1: evaluate at every integer storm age, linear interpolation of x,y,r,I between the 2-s storm observations; each integer age counts 1 s. obs2 (2-s obs only, each counts 2 s) is a cheaper live variant.

nowcast.target: Y = E[exp(-O_rest/120)] for the current storm; FV = 32 + 18*(1 - exp(-(O_prev_storms + O_so_far)/120) * Y * prod_{future rounds} m_r)
nowcast.feature_defs: DR = dead-reckoning remaining weighted closure (current x,y; velocity = displacement over last 10 s; r,I constant; I decays linearly to 0 from age 420 to 480; 2-s steps). CONE = same along the latest official cone (current position then cone points; extrapolate last segment). GP = sum_island (grid weight on island) * official P(hurricane conditions). CL = weight of substations closed now. p_<island> = official P(hurricane conditions). outlook_<k> = 1 if latest official outlook is k (erratic = all zero). Before the first advisory (age<30) only [1, exp(-DR/c), CL] are used. Use the coefficient row of the latest age bucket <= current age; clip Y to [0,1].

GEN.closure_integration_recommended: cont: between consecutive 2-s storm observations interpolate x, y, radius, intensity linearly; integrate closure with the midpoint rule at dt <= 0.25 s (0.1 s used); substation i closed while I*exp(-(d_i/r)^2) > 0.35; O += w_i*dt. Live: each segment [t, t+2] is integrable as soon as the observation at t+2 arrives.

future_storms.note: m_r = E[exp(-X_r/c)] over training storms of round r. Simple FV before round k: a + b*(1 - exp(-D/c)*prod_{r>=k} m_r) (method A, ignores depletion of remaining value; biased low for RECON/MAT). Better (method B): resample the training seasons' fresh damage fractions f = pct/(100 - prior cumulative pct) for the remaining rounds and apply them to the current remaining value of each company; GEN outage is not depleted (cross-round corr ~0), use method A for GEN.
future_storms.method_B_algorithm: For each training season row and each remaining round r>=k: for each company, add_pct = remaining_pct * f[r-1][company]; remaining_pct -= add_pct; accumulate driver $ (RECON: 9P+7G+1.2F; MAT: 9P+6I+2.5A+7G+1.2F). FV = a + b*(1 - mean_rows exp(-(D_now + added)/c)).
future_storms.pattern_tables_note: m_by_pattern and realtime.gen_m_rest_by_age_and_true_pattern are keyed on the manifest TRUE pattern, which a live bot never observes. Use them only mixed with a live pattern posterior (from official/wire outlooks), never with the true pattern.

prelim_vs_final.note: 'calib' was fit on all 1800 storms (includes holdout); use calib_train_only. Neither raw nor calibrated preliminary beats the house on round-3 holdout (RECON 0.70 raw / 0.74 calibrated vs house 0.43; MAT 0.35 / 0.36 vs 0.20).

realtime.house_row_label_note: In realtime_results the house keys '738' and '778' are actually real seconds 730 and 770 (px5 grid floors to 10 s). The true row 369 (738 s) gives RECON 0.411, MAT 0.195, GEN 0.060 rmse over all 600; the house reflects the final report from row 372 (744 s), i.e. about 4 s after 740 s.

alternatives_checked.measure: impact count weighted by island grid weight

house_bias_all600: house consensus minus settlement at round opens: RECON +0.57/+0.47/+0.30 (se .18/.15/.11), MAT +0.22/+0.17/+0.13 (se .07/.06/.05), GEN +0.22/+0.13/+0.09 (se .10/.08/.06) for rounds 1/2/3; after the round-3 final report the house is unbiased with sd 0.08 RECON, 0.05 MAT, 0.06 GEN

house_bias_split.definition: mean(house consensus at round-k open - settlement), se, t
house_bias_split.note: The pooled all-600 numbers in house_bias_all600 mix the fit period with the holdout. Out of sample the bias is about one third of the in-sample value and not significant (t <= 1.1). Treat a short lean as at most +0.2/share for RECON, +0.08 for MAT, +0.05 for GEN, and size it accordingly.

verification.by: independent verifier, scripts in work/se/verify-rebuild (vextract, vrecon, vrecon2, vgen_feat, vgen_fit, vgen_fine, vgen_fine_fit, vgen_check, vgen_var, vimpact, vhouse, vprelim, vcond, vnowcast, vnowcast2, vfinal)
corrections: GEN: use continuous-time (fine-step) closure integration instead of int1: holdout rmse 0.0220 / max 0.082 vs 0.0251 / 0.120 (fields GEN.closure_integration_recommended, params_fitted_cont, *_cont).
House open bias: replace pooled all-600 figures with the split (house_bias_split); out-of-sample t <= 1.1.
Prelim calibration: refit on training storms only (calib_train_only).
True-pattern lookup tables flagged as not live-usable directly (future_storms.pattern_tables_note).
